work.author: Gregory of Nyssa
work.description: Gregory of Nyssa's treatise on the making of man, written about 379 for his brother Peter as the supplement his brother Basil's Hexaemeron left undone: the Hexaemeron breaks off at the sixth day before the creation of man, and this work expounds what Basil did not reach. It is a treatise in thirty chapters preceded by a dedicatory letter, and its scriptural subject is the divine utterance of Genesis 1:26 and its accomplishment in 1:27.
work.title: De hominis opificio
